errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the average rate from the instant to a slightly later time gives the same number; a student who expects it to holds that a rate belongs to an interval, while one who sees it change reached for the nearest available average.
errors.name: Average rate over an interval reported as the rate at an instant
non_conceptual_causes: the average rate over a named interval is the only rate computation available before the derivative
the starting time is the only other input the problem supplies
the question read as asking for the rate up to that instant
errors.notes: Minted 2026-09-28 in stage 15 for the productive-failure opener BC-QA-02014, whose first distractor it names. CHA-2 separates rates over intervals from rates at an instant (ced:60).
errors.observed_behavior: Asked for the rate of change at one instant, the response divides the change over a whole interval, usually from the starting time to that instant, by the length of the interval and reports that average.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value reported is an average rate over an interval, so an answer point for the rate at the instant is not earned.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate the proposed antiderivative and compare it with the integrand; one who expects the check to succeed holds the rule wrongly, while one who spots the stray factor made a slip.
errors.name: Power rule for antiderivatives applied with the wrong divisor
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative power rule, which multiplies by the old exponent, run backwards by rote
the division carried out on the first term and forgotten on the later ones
a negative or fractional new exponent avoided as a divisor
errors.notes: Minted 2026-09-28 in stage 15 for BC-QA-06019, whose two power-rule distractors it names; FUN-6.C.2 ties antiderivatives to the differentiation rules (ced:125).
errors.observed_behavior: The response raises each exponent by one but does not divide by the new exponent, or divides by the old exponent instead.
errors.scoring_consequence: The proposed function does not differentiate to the integrand, so an antiderivative point is not earned.
